newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent falls on paper market, easy on pbysica.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent falls on paper market, easy on pbysica.

text.p: North Sea Brent eased on a quiet paper market on Tuesday with outright levels, intermonth spreads and contracts for difference falling, traders said.
No physical deals were reported early with most European traders returning to work after Monday's Pentacost holiday.
Traders said Dated Brent was assessed at July Brent -20/25 cents, steady to a little easier than a deal on Monday at July Brent -20 cents.
"I think the value (of Brent) is somewhere between July Brent -20 and -25 (cents)," a European major said. "There really isn't that much lively talk, we've had surprisingly few calls."
The paper market was equally quiet, with very thin talk.
July Brent was 20 cents a barrel down at $19.96 by 1110 GMT.
Traders said crude fell on poor refinery margins which could result in poor crude demand, and fears of a pre-expiry jump on June NYMEX crude.
Brent intermonth spreads eased, with Jun/Jul very thinly talked at -5/0 cents from 1/3 cents late on Monday and Jul/Aug offered five cents lower at -2 cents.
Brent CFDs were largely quiet, with Jun 9-13 offered three cents weaker at July Brent -23 cents. One Brent was in the chains, a cargo five o'clocked on Friday that won a deferral.
Other North Sea grades were also thinly talked early on Tuesday. One major seller started to show its early June barrels of Norwegian crudes but no bids have been made yet.
The Norwegian major also said it had two unsold May cargoes on offer, an Ekofisk at Dated Brent +15/20 cents, a little easier than its earlier levels, and an Oseberg whose price was negotiable.
There was unconfirmed talk of an end May Ekofisk co-loaded by a trading house and a Wall Street trader and a Gullfaks cargo sold recently but no further details were available.
